title: Does the core's effect grow with position? Position analysis of the fixed-trace dumps, and the vLLM fork with q_b and the output projections in BF16 together
question: On the 93 fixed science-question traces, does the core's effect on next-token distributions or on the stop decision build up with position, and do q_b and the output projections in BF16 together move the stop decision?
engines: tpurtell vLLM fork v0.9.2-experimental image with the local loader modification (repro/vllm-k6-loader; not a tpurtell release)
tpurtell/cuteafd v4.0.0 (stored core-swap dumps, the refused C-K6a launch and the C-K6 recheck; image digest as in results/2026-11-03-cuteafd-core-swap)

goals.question: Does the divergence between arms (top-64 KL to the 6-bit core) grow with position along the trace, for any core group, on either engine?

design.instrument: per-row top-64 KL(ref ‖ arm); per-trace OLS slope of KL on log2(position), mean over traces; pooled KL by position bin
arms: vLLM G2 dumps: each group arm vs k6; noise reference k6r2 vs k6
CuteAFD core-swap step 2 dumps: core (C-K6x vs C-K6), experts (C-K4 vs C-K6x), launch (C-K6r2 vs C-K6)

design.repeats: existing launches (vLLM: one per arm + k6r2; CuteAFD: bit-identical launches)

goals.headline: Exploratory. Divergence does not grow with position for any group on either engine: every swap arm's KL to the 6-bit core is highest in the first 1K rows, flat from 1K to 64K, lower beyond 64K; attention groups look like the controls; k6r2 and lm_head flat. On CuteAFD, core M1 slope minus experts +0.019 [+0.002, +0.047] (the core's divergence falls less with position than the experts').

goals.headline: Exploratory; met the trigger written before computing. CuteAFD core (BF16-core side minus 6-bit) +0.057 [+0.011, +0.104], slope +0.033 per doubling [+0.020, +0.046]; experts slope -0.038 [-0.056, -0.015] (opposite). On vLLM the whole-core swap goes the other way (-0.116 [-0.148, -0.092]) and lm_head alone -0.069. The run notes the measure was not in the frozen protocol and weights rows where p(</think>) is ~1e-6.
goals.replication: opposite signs on the two engines again in 2026-11-06-new-questions/DESC-SCORE (vLLM -0.114, CuteAFD +0.106)
goals.status_note: NOTE.md:34 and 2026-11-06-new-questions/NQ-RESULT.md:23 give the vLLM whole-core value as -0.116; analysis/POSITION.json /vllm/all/m2_last512_logp_delta is -0.11549, which rounds to -0.115 (the findings use the data value).

goals.status_note: README.md:14-15 directs reading with 2026-11-06-new-questions, where the shift does not appear on 30 new questions. The arm was frozen before its launch, but the layout it tests was chosen after reading the G2 screen's two lp_close flags (2 of 27 group tests) and was measured on the same 11 questions: a post hoc lead tested on its own data.
goals.headline: Frozen reading: lp_close, qbo minus K4-Core-K6 (launch means), +0.0118 [+0.0047, +0.0205] clustered by question; +0.0118 [+0.0009, +0.0225] over traces; within-arm launch differences k6 -0.0018, qbo -0.0007; all four cross-launch pairings positive (+0.0106 to +0.0131): supported under the rule written before the launch. Size about a 1.2% relative change in p(</think>) at the close. vLLM fork v0.9.2-experimental + route b, 11 science-question questions.
